description: AGS Beers Criteria 2023 for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults

rules.message: AGS Beers Criteria: First-generation antihistamines should be avoided in older adults (>=65). Highly anticholinergic; clearance reduced; severe risk of cognitive decline, acute confusion, delirium, urinary retention, and falls.

citations: By the 2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria Update Expert Panel. American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081.

rules.message: AGS Beers Criteria: Tertiary amine tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) should be avoided in older adults (>=65). Potent anticholinergic and alpha-adrenergic blockade causes profound sedation, syncope, and orthostatic falls.

citations: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081.

rules.message: AGS Beers Criteria: Oral antimuscarinics for overactive bladder carry significant anticholinergic burden in older adults (>=65), aggravating dementia symptoms and precipitating urinary retention.

citations: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081.

rules.message: AGS Beers Criteria: Benzodiazepines should be avoided in older adults (>=65). Older adults have increased sensitivity and decreased metabolism, leading to prolonged ataxia, motor vehicle crashes, and fractures.

citations: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081.
